Trace and nontrace VM execution wrappers that include the shared interpreter core.

# Purpose
This C file defines two entry points for executing an `fd_vm_t` virtual machine: [`fd_vm_exec_notrace`](<#fd_vm_exec_notrace>) and [`fd_vm_exec_trace`](<#fd_vm_exec_trace>). Both functions prepare the local variables required by the shared interpreter template `fd_vm_interp_core.c`, then include that file to run the VM execution loop. The code reads execution state from the `vm` object, including `text`, `text_cnt`, `entry_pc`, `calldests`, `syscalls`, memory region tables, registers, and the shadow state, and returns an error code in `err`.

The two functions differ only in tracing mode. [`fd_vm_exec_notrace`](<#fd_vm_exec_notrace>) disables execution and memory tracing by undefining `FD_VM_INTERP_EXE_TRACING_ENABLED` and `FD_VM_INTERP_MEM_TRACING_ENABLED` before including the interpreter core. [`fd_vm_exec_trace`](<#fd_vm_exec_trace>) defines both macros before inclusion, so the same interpreter template runs with trace output enabled. This file therefore provides the VM execution interface and selects between traced and non-traced execution without duplicating the interpreter logic.
